claim: The cold-start benchmark is now a surface rather than a script: 175 questions in four tiers with conjunctive gates, a result contract with 38 cases proving twelve refusals, a JSON manifest a fresh model can read without opening the source, an answer-stripped paper, run records that make yesterday and today comparable, a daily agent workflow and a disabled schedule. Seven independent witness passes each defeated it, all seventy-four findings one class - a check reading a declaration where it could compute or look up the value - and the seventh named the generator: the record supplied its own referents. What needs your judgement is two things: the AI-native assessment of this surface reads OPEN because earn_it is yours, and whether seven adversarial passes on one bounded concern was a resource commitment you would have authorised.

visible_result.shows: the run-record contract graded against its own defeating cases, and the corpus checked for questions that cannot be scored
visible_result.expect: PASS: 34 run-record case(s), 11 refusal(s) all proven, corpus structurally sound. Then `python scripts/sov_coldstart.py describe` prints the surface manifest as JSON, and `python scripts/sov_coldstart.py --record run` takes a full reading in about two minutes. Expect the verdict UNPROVEN and a handful of DRIFT lines: 18 of the 49 tier 0 questions are prose only you can grade, so the tier 0 gate cannot be fully run without you, and the counts a repository moves daily drift by design. The MATCH and DRIFT totals are deliberately not stated here - they move every day, and a packet that pins them would read as a failure the first time you ran it. `python scripts/sov_coldstart.py history` shows the recorded runs and refuses to diff two runs taken under different coverage.

evidence.says: the result shape: which corpus at which digest, which commit, which participant, what each tier scored, and standing pinned to BUILT by const

34 cases proving all eleven refusals fire. D-001 is the obvious attack, an honest tier table with ADMISSIBLE written at the bottom; D-012, D-014, D-022 and D-029 are four the witnesses found - a table that supplies its own gate, a table with the tier 0 row deleted, a record whose owner verdict file never existed, and one whose verdict file names a grader in no principal registry

grade_row computes one tier's gate and result from its counts, tally builds the table, derive turns the table into a verdict; the printed card and the record grader call the same three, so there is one gate table and no second opinion about it
defects recomputes the verdict from the record's own numbers and refuses a record that states a different one; write refuses to write a defective record at all
104 cases, including all six witnesses' attacks kept verbatim; scripts/tests/test_pinned_glob.py adds ten more that grade the glob matcher against git rather than against its own intent
the AI-native reading: reachability PARTIAL, commitment PARTIAL, provenance PARTIAL, retraction NONE, one qualification PASS and eight UNPROVEN, earn_it OPEN
the daily agent path: fetch the paper once, hand each section to a fresh agent told not to read any file, grade the merged answers, record both readings
three rulings, five scoring rules that were each an exploit first, the defaults taken, and four things this does not fix
ten mutations, each disabling one check and asserting the declared corpus notices; it found on its first run that no case reached the answers-shape check, which selfcheck had been reporting as proven
REFUSED to record this run: CORPUS_NOT_AT_REVISION - the corpus is not reachable from the commit the record names, so the run cannot be recorded until this concern lands

why_it_matters: Every launched agent in this repository is oriented by CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and the session hooks before it reads a single file, and those pages go stale silently. sov_snapshot.py checks whether the page matches the repository; it cannot check what a fresh participant actually believes after reading it, which is the thing that decides whether an agent does the right thing in its first ten minutes. This measures that, records it, and can be pointed at a fresh agent daily. It also earned its keep during construction: adversarial readers asked to beat it found three places where a rule this repository states in prose had no mechanism behind it, which is packet A10.
what_could_defeat_it: A participant scoring ADMISSIBLE on answers it read out of corpus.json, and a change landing on that basis. The paper verb removes the reason to read the key; it cannot stop it, and that is recorded as not fixed rather than mitigated.

A daily run whose drift is dominated by counts that move for reasons no reader cares about. The corpus would then be measuring repository churn rather than orientation accuracy and tier 2 would need re-cutting.
A participant scoring well and then making an error the benchmark claims to cover. That would mean it measures recall rather than competence.

Evidence that the corpus itself encodes a rule wrongly. Tier 0 questions assert doctrine, so a wrong tier 0 expectation teaches every future participant the wrong rule with the full weight of a failed gate behind it.
residuals: Seven independent witness passes, seven defeats, seventy-four findings: 1, 7, 8, 16, 10, 11, 16. Four of the seven found a defect the previous pass's repair introduced. The seventh named the generator - the record supplied its own referents, so each repair bound one more by digest and the hole moved one field over - and decisions/0078 Rulings 4 and 5 are the shape change that follows from it. I stopped the passes there rather than taking an eighth, which is an ordinary resource judgement I made and you may disagree with.

The largest thing still open: selfcheck is the participant grading a fixture it ships with. AGENTS.md puts cross-participant cases in conformance/ with an oracle that does not import participant code; here the fixture is data under conformance/ and the grader is the thing graded. test_fixture_coverage.py narrows that and does not close it, and closing it means a second independent implementation of the record grader.

The daily workflow had never run. Three of its prompts told an agent to run a command with a sentence period on the end, which exits 2, so the whole path returned 'the paper could not be fetched'. reports/coldstart/ holds INTEGRITY records and no COMPETENCE record, because that path could not execute. Fixed, and still unexercised end to end: running it spends agent budget, which is your call rather than mine.

A peer session found four diagrams pinning a STATUS.yaml digest matching no committed version of the file, from a builder run in the shared tree. A run record had the same hole: two records under reports/coldstart/ name commit cc95d85 with different corpus digests. CORPUS_NOT_AT_REVISION now compares the digest against the corpus blob at the named commit, so no run can be recorded until this work is committed. That is the correct behaviour and it means the six existing records are not reproducible by anyone but this disk.

Five of the six records under reports/coldstart/ fail RUN_ID_NOT_DERIVED when read by today's checker, because run_identity gained a field after they were written. The identity scheme is not versioned, so changing it silently invalidates every record ever written. I have not repaired this: versioning the scheme changes the schema and re-derives all 38 fixture ids, which is real scope at the end of a presented concern. I left the six records in place rather than deleting them, because they are the evidence for the residual above.
The corpus ships its own answers inside the repository under test. Closing that means holding the key outside the tree, which is a change to where the corpus lives and is a separate concern.

57 of the 175 questions are prose that a string comparison cannot judge. They read UNGRADED until you write a verdict file, so an unattended daily run will normally record UNPROVEN. That is the honest state, not a fault, but it means the cadence measures the deterministic 118 and parks the rest.
Time to useful and intervention count are not measured, so cold_start_competence stays UNPROVEN in the assessment rather than moving to PASS.

contracts/ai-native-qualifications.json still evidences cold_start_competence with FOUND-009, which is about Sov's bounded agency and measures neither. Repointing it crosses into the contract decision 0070 owns and was left alone.

The selfcheck reaches verify.py through run_tooling_tests.py rather than as its own named check, because scripts/sovverify/checks.py is exactly at the 300-line module ceiling and four other live sessions hold that file. Splitting the check table is the verification domain's concern.

Two corpus expectations, E02 (skills on disk) and E04 (schedule declarations), drifted because this change added one of each. They were deliberately not rebased: rebasing to uncommitted state was a mistake made earlier in this concern and caught, so they stay drifted until the work lands.

The witness could not write its observation. The sov-witness role under .claude/agents/ carries no Write tool and it declined to use Bash to get around that, which is correct. So this concern has an independent reading and no independent record of one, and the builder transcribing that prose into a file is exactly the seam authority.py names. Whether a witness should hold Write is a harness question nobody has been asked.

python scripts/verify.py exits 1 on six checks, all red before this work. The builder's claim that none involves a path here was too flat: documentation reader and diagram provenance would be red anyway and this concern also contributes, because four of its .md files are in the published corpus and absent from the built page and its STATUS.yaml edit moves a digest diagrams/authority-typing.md declares.

The gate covering this contract grades bytes that are not in the repository. run_tooling_tests.py discovers test modules by globbing the filesystem, and every file in this concern is untracked, so a checkout of HEAD would pass with zero coverage of the run-record contract and say nothing about it. That resolves the moment the work lands, and until then the green is about this working tree only.

A third failing check this concern contributes to, which an earlier residual missed: repository tooling tests fails partly through test_sov_docs, which asserts the same sov_docs.cmd_check the documentation-reader failure already conceded. And all four stale diagrams are stale for the STATUS.yaml edit, not one.

The fifth pass found that SELF_GRADED checked two files agreed rather than that a second party graded, so a participant that wrote both files and named itself the grader passed. It is now resolved against contracts/principals.json under the ruling decisions/0070 already made. That is a floor: the registry grants nothing, and anyone who can write it can add an entry. decisions/0075, in packet A10, is what keeps that file outside the standing grant.

No owner verdict file exists, and the fixture that stood in for one is now a defeating case. Until you grade the 57 prose questions, every competence run records UNPROVEN by design, and 18 of those 57 are tier 0.
on_accept: The benchmark stands as the way cold-start orientation is measured here, the eleven refusals become the contract a run record is held to, and the daily schedule is available to enable whenever you want it firing. Judging earn_it on conformance/assessments/cold-start-benchmark.json is a separate act you can take at any time; until you do, the assessment reads OPEN by design.
on_reject: Say which of the three rulings in decisions/0078 is wrong. Ruling 3, that the verdict is derived and never written, is the one everything else hangs on: without it a run record is a participant's opinion of itself. Reverting is deleting scripts/sovcoldstart/, scripts/sov_coldstart.py, two contracts, one fixture corpus, three harness files, two test modules and reports/coldstart/; nothing existing was weakened and no check was loosened.
